5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
5.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

6.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
6.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

7.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

8.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
8.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

9.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'they did good / acted well / did beautifully'. The core sense ('iḥsān') is doing a thing excellently and beautifully, and also conferring kindness and benefit on others.
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in a derived (augmented) pattern meaning 'to do well, do good'. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did…'). (The trailing silent alif is a spelling convention after plural -ū.)
10.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
12.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

13.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
13.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
13.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

14.meaning: "A good thing / a benefit" — something good, beautiful, or pleasing; a good deed or a piece of good fortune.
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective. The -at ending marks it as feminine; the final -un is nominative case with tanwīn (the -n showing it is indefinite, 'a good thing'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence.
14.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

15.meaning: "and indeed the abode / home of…" — an emphatic phrase naming a dwelling place or final abode; 'dār' is a house, home, or realm one settles in, and the word is often used for the lasting abode of the Hereafter.
15.grammar: Combines the connector wa- ('and') with the emphasising la- ('surely/indeed'), which stresses what follows. 'Dāru' is a noun, and its -u ending is the subject/naming (nominative) case, typically marking it as the topic or doer; here it is also in a possessive link, so it is normally completed by a following 'of…' noun.
15.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, circle, revolve; a dwelling one returns to

16.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
16.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
16.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

17.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
17.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
17.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

18.meaning: And how excellent indeed! — an exclamation of praise: 'what a fine / excellent thing it is!' A fixed verb of commendation used to extol something as truly good, here emphasized.

parts.en: how excellent it is (verb of praise)

18.grammar: A frozen verb of praise, niʿma ('how excellent / good is…'), used to commend something. It does not inflect for tense in the usual way; the la- prefix adds emphasis ('truly, indeed') and wa- joins it as 'and'. It is the positive counterpart of bi'sa ('how wretched').
18.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — favor, grace, goodness; to be excellent/pleasant

19.meaning: A noun meaning 'abode', 'dwelling', or 'home' — a place of residence and settling; used for a lasting dwelling-place, including the eternal Hereafter.
19.grammar: A noun bearing the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence or the predicate in a statement of identity ('X will be the abode'). It frequently heads a possessive phrase ('the abode OF …').
19.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, encircle; a dwelling enclosed by walls

20.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

20.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.

1.meaning: Gardens — lush, densely shaded enclosures whose foliage covers the ground; the plural of the word for a garden, used pre-eminently for the Gardens of Paradise.
1.grammar: A feminine sound plural of 'janna' (garden), formed with the '-āt' plural ending. The final '-u' is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun that simply names or identifies something ('… are gardens').
1.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; lush garden whose growth covers the earth

2.meaning: Perpetual residence, lasting settlement — an abode of permanence and enduring stay; classically a proper name for the Gardens of eternal dwelling.
2.grammar: A verbal noun used as a name for a place of permanent dwelling. The ending -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn): the -i vowel typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition, while the final -n signals that it is indefinite.

3.meaning: They enter it / they will enter it. The verb expresses going in or passing into a place, with an attached object meaning 'it' (a feminine thing or place).
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('ya-' = 'they'), with the '-ūna' indicative ending (here written '-ū-na-hā'). The attached '-hā' is an object pronoun meaning 'it/her/them (feminine)', so the whole means 'they enter it'. The plain indicative signals an ongoing or future action.

4.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
6.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

7.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
7.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.
7.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — river, flowing water

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
9.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: They will / they wish — to want, will, or desire something; an act of the will choosing or intending that a thing be.
11.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they will / they wish'), and -ūna also signals the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact).
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish, want; thing

12.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
12.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
12.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

13.meaning: "He rewards / requites / repays" — to give back a fitting return for deeds, whether reward or recompense. The verb jazā means to recompense, to pay back what is due for an action.
13.grammar: This is a present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he"), so it means "he rewards/requites." The final long -ī belongs to the verb's stem (a verb whose root ends in a weak letter).
13.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, reward, requite, pay back what is due

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
14.root: — (proper divine name)

15.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

15.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.
15.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (oneself)

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: It/they take them fully — to take a soul completely and in full at the moment of death; literally 'to receive in full / exact in full', used of the angels or of Allah taking the soul wholly when life ends. The accompanying 'them' is the object.

parts.en: take in full, take in death (Form V stem)

2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix (third-person feminine singular, also used for a non-human plural subject such as 'the angels'). The attached -humu means 'them' as the direct object. Form V (tawaffā) gives the sense of taking something completely for oneself.
2.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfill, complete, pay in full; to take in full

3.meaning: The angels — the heavenly beings created by Allah to carry out His commands. A definite plural noun referring to that order of spiritual creatures.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun (a 'broken' plural of malak, 'angel'), treated grammatically as feminine. The prefixed al- means 'the.' The final -u marks the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence.
3.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — possession, dominion; also linked to أ-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) 'to convey a message'; malak = angel

4.meaning: Pure, wholesome, good ones — those who are clean, sound, and morally untainted; 'good' in the sense of pure and pleasant, free of corruption.
4.grammar: A plural adjective/noun describing persons ('pure, good ones'). The -īna ending marks masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used for a direct object, after a preposition, or as a descriptive state (e.g. 'while being pure').
4.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, wholesome, pleasant

5.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

6.meaning: Peace, soundness, safety, well-being — freedom from harm and discord; a word of greeting and of the wholeness and security that comes from being safe and at peace.
6.grammar: A noun. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative: the -u marks the nominative (the form a subject or a stated/announced word takes), and the final -n ('tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('peace', not 'the peace').

7.meaning: 'Upon / over you (plural)' — the preposition 'on, over, upon' with an attached 'you all' pronoun, indicating something coming onto or directed at a group.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -kum addresses a group ('you all'); the final -u (kumu) is a connecting helper-vowel easing the link into a following word that starts with the definite article. The preposition conveys 'on' or 'over'.
7.root: — (preposition; relates to ع-ل-و, height/elevation)

8.meaning: 'Enter!' — a command to a group to go into or enter a place.
8.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, enter!'). The initial alif is a helping-vowel prefix that lets the word begin (pronounced 'u-' here), needed because the stem would otherwise start with a vowelless consonant. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

9.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
9.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.
9.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
10.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
11.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

12.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
12.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
1.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

2.meaning: They look toward, watch for, or await; a present-tense act of a group either gazing at something or expecting/waiting for it to happen.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). The full -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action that is happening or habitual.

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: 'That it comes to them / that it should come to them' — a 'to come, to arrive, to reach' verb with an attached 'them,' expressing the coming or arrival of something upon people. The final -a vowel reflects a subjunctive mood, typically after a particle like 'that' or 'until.'
5.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she comes'). The final -a is the subjunctive mood ending, the form taken after particles meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or 'until.' The suffix -hum(u) is the object 'them' (the -u is a connecting vowel before the next word).

6.meaning: The angels — the heavenly beings created by Allah to carry out His commands. A definite plural noun referring to that order of spiritual creatures.
6.grammar: A definite plural noun (a 'broken' plural of malak, 'angel'), treated grammatically as feminine. The prefixed al- means 'the.' The final -u marks the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence.
6.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — possession, dominion; also linked to أ-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) 'to convey a message'; malak = angel

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: He/it comes, brings, or arrives — to come or to bring (something) about. The form points to an action not yet completed (present or future).
8.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it comes'). The ya- prefix (a single, undoubled yāʾ) marks a single male/thing subject. The final -a (in -iya) is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that', 'until', or 'so that', giving the sense '… that he come' or '… until he comes'.

9.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
9.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; an affair/matter

10.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
10.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
10.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

11.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
11.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

12.meaning: He did / he acted / he committed — he carried out a deed. A general verb for performing or bringing about an action.

parts.en: he did / did it (he/it, masculine singular, past)

12.grammar: A simple past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular. The third-person masculine singular has no separate suffix; the bare stem ending in -a expresses 'he did' as a completed action.
12.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, to act, to make

13.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
13.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
14.root: — (preposition)

15.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
15.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
15.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

16.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
16.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

17.meaning: 'He wronged them / treated them unjustly' — to place something where it does not belong, to oppress or deal unfairly. An attached pronoun marks the wronged party.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb (third-person singular masculine, 'he did…'). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel appears here as -humu (an extra short u) to ease pronunciation before a following word. Past tense states a completed action.
17.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to do wrong, oppress, act unjustly; darkness/misplacement

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
19.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

20.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
20.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

21.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
21.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

22.meaning: 'They wrong / they do wrong' — to act unjustly or oppressively, presented as an ongoing or repeated action. The same root pictures putting things out of their proper place.
22.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine 'they' doing the action now or habitually ('they wrong / keep wronging'). The full -ūna ending (with its final -na) is the mark of the ordinary, uninterrupted present tense for a plural subject.

1.meaning: So it struck / befell them — to hit the mark, reach, and afflict; (of a calamity or consequence) to come upon and strike someone. The 'so/then' links it as a result, and 'them' is the object reached.

parts.en: to strike / befall / reach (Form IV stem)

1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb meaning a completed action by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it struck'), prefixed with fa- ('so/then'). The attached -hum means 'them' as the direct object. Form IV (aṣāba) carries the sense of hitting the target or making something befall.
1.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, be correct; (Form IV) to strike, befall, afflict

2.meaning: Evil deeds / evil consequences — bad actions and the harmful results they bring; misdeeds, offenses, and the afflictions that issue from them. The plural of a word denoting a bad or harmful thing.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun. The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically identifies the noun as the subject (the doer or topic) of its clause. Being grammatically incomplete on its own, it commonly stands in a possessive link with a following noun ('the evil deeds of …').
2.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil; to harm

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
4.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

5.meaning: And it closed in / encompassed — to surround completely and descend upon, especially of a punishment or consequence that envelops people and leaves no escape.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb (a hollow root, whose middle letter appears as the long 'ā'). It is third-person masculine singular ('he/it did') and complete in the past; it characteristically governs a following 'with/upon' to name those whom the encirclement befalls. The prefixed wa- simply means 'and.'

6.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
6.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

7.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
7.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
7.root: — (particle; no root)

8.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
8.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: 'They mock / ridicule / hold in derision.' The ongoing or habitual act of making a mockery of someone, scoffing and jeering at them.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb of Form X (the ista-/-stah- pattern). The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural acting in the present or habitual ('they keep mocking'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative (uninterrupted) mood. The Form X shape here intensifies the sense of deliberately making a mockery.
10.root: ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ) — to mock, ridicule, scoff, deride

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they associated partners / they set up partners (with Allah)' — to ascribe partners or equals to Allah, the act underlying idolatry and polytheism.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern meaning 'to make (someone) a partner'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural subject, 'they', so it reads 'they associated partners (with Allah)'.

4.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
5.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: We worshipped / served — to worship, devote oneself in humble servitude, and obey; the act of a servant submitting to and venerating the One served. With the 'we' ending it states that this devotion was done by the speakers.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the suffix -nā marking a first-person plural subject ('we worshipped / served'). It denotes a completed action carried out by the speakers.
8.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a servant

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
9.root: — (preposition)

10.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

10.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
11.root: — (preposition)

12.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
12.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

13.meaning: The detached pronoun 'we' — standing alone to name or emphasize the speakers as a group ('we ourselves').
13.grammar: An independent (standalone) personal pronoun meaning 'we'. Such detached pronouns are not inflected for case; they serve as the subject of a sentence or add emphasis ('it is we who…'). The fixed final '-u' is simply part of the pronoun's form. (The doubling shown on the opening nūn reflects assimilation in connected recitation with a preceding word, not a change in the pronoun itself.)

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: Our fathers and forefathers; our ancestors. The word points to the line of male forebears whose example or tradition is often invoked.
15.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our') attached. The plural ends in a hamza (written here on a 'wāw' seat as 'ؤ'), and the '-u' vowel on it before the pronoun is nominative, the case typically used when the noun is the subject (the doer) of a sentence.
15.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — father, fatherhood

16.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: 'We forbade / made unlawful' — to declare something prohibited and off-limits, treating it as sacred or forbidden so that it may not be approached or used.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (denoting decisive, complete prohibition). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', so the whole means 'we made unlawful / we forbade'. Being past tense, it reports a completed act.
17.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, to make sacred/inviolable; the forbidden and the sacrosanct

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

19.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
22.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
22.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

23.meaning: He did / he acted / he committed — he carried out a deed. A general verb for performing or bringing about an action.

parts.en: he did / did it (he/it, masculine singular, past)

23.grammar: A simple past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular. The third-person masculine singular has no separate suffix; the bare stem ending in -a expresses 'he did' as a completed action.
23.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, to act, to make

24.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
24.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

26.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
26.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
26.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

27.meaning: 'So/then — is it the case that…?' A linking 'then' joined to an interrogative particle that introduces a yes/no question, often carrying a sense of urging, challenge, or expectation ('will you not…?').
27.grammar: A compound of the connective fa- ('so, then', linking to what precedes) and the question particle hal, which turns a statement into a yes/no question and frequently implies expectation or exhortation. Particles like this are invariable — they take no case or mood ending.

28.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
28.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
28.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

29.meaning: 'the messengers' — the envoys sent by Allah, taken definitely as a known group.
29.grammar: The prefix al- ('the') makes it definite (its 'l' assimilates to the following 'r'). The base is the broken plural of rasūl. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the messengers') or follows a preposition.

30.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
30.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

31.meaning: The conveying / the delivering (of a message): the act of passing on and communicating something so it reaches its hearers fully and clearly; a verbal noun naming that act.
31.grammar: A definite verbal noun (a noun naming an action) with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('… is …').
31.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, to arrive at; to convey

32.meaning: Clear, plain, manifest; that which makes things evident — both 'clearly apparent in itself' and 'making the truth clear to others'.
32.grammar: An active participle, 'the one that makes clear / the manifest', from a causative (form-IV) pattern, carried by the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word serves as a subject or as a descriptor of such a word.

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent/raised up — to dispatch or commission someone (especially to send a messenger); the root also carries the sense of stirring up or raising to life.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending means 'we' and marks a completed past action ('we sent'). The ending is the subject-marker for a first-person plural that has acted.
2.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send forth, dispatch, raise up, resurrect

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
4.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

5.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
5.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

6.meaning: A messenger — one who is sent bearing a message; an envoy or apostle dispatched to deliver and convey what the sender entrusts.
6.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a messenger'). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a/an') and the accusative case, which usually shows the noun is a direct object or otherwise governed into that case.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, one sent

7.meaning: That — an explanatory particle introducing the content of a preceding statement or command, roughly 'namely that …' or 'to the effect that …'. It unpacks what was said or commanded.
7.grammar: An explanatory particle 'an' meaning 'that / namely,' used to spell out the substance of a foregoing verb of saying or commanding (so the words that follow explain it). Its base form ends in a vowel-less 'n'; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant, not a case ending.

8.meaning: 'Serve!,' 'worship!,' 'devote yourselves in obedience!' — a command to render worship and humble service. The underlying sense is to submit oneself wholly, in reverence and obedience, to the one served.
8.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending means the order is given to several people: 'you all do it!' The initial vowel is a helping prosthetic vowel that lets the word begin, since the bare command stem would otherwise start with a vowelless letter.
8.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, devotion

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
9.root: — (proper name)

10.meaning: And avoid / shun! — a command to a group to keep away from, steer clear of, and stay on one side away from something; to give it a wide berth.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group, joined by 'and'. The -ū ending directs the order at a masculine plural 'you' ('you all, avoid!'). The initial helping vowel (i-) appears because the stem would otherwise begin with a consonant cluster. Form VIII here conveys deliberately keeping oneself away.
10.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; to keep to one side of, avoid

11.meaning: 'The false god / idol / that which is wrongly worshipped' — a term (from the root meaning 'to overstep all bounds, transgress in tyranny') for any object of worship set up beside Allah: an idol, a tyrant, a devil, or any false deity that leads people into rebellion.

parts.en: false deity / idol / object of false worship

11.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a vowel marks the accusative case — the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb (the thing worshipped/served).
11.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all limits, be tyrannical, transgress

12.meaning: "so / and among them / of them (there are)" — the preposition min ('from, among, of') with the pronoun 'them', expressing 'among them' or 'some of them', introduced by 'so/and'.
12.grammar: A connective particle plus a preposition with an attached pronoun. Fa- means 'so/and then', linking to what precedes. Min ('from/among') takes no case ending; the suffix -hum is 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The phrase often introduces a partition ('among them are…').

13.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
13.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

14.meaning: He guided, led aright, showed the way; to direct someone toward a goal or onto the right path. Of Allah, it denotes granting guidance to truth and faith.

parts.en: he (past-tense ending, with weak final letter)

14.grammar: A past/perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he guided'). This is a 'defective' verb whose third root letter is a weak letter, so the final syllable appears as a long -ā (written with alif maqṣūra ى). The past tense states a completed action. With no attached subject pronoun, it simply means 'he/it guided'.
14.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right way

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
15.root: — (proper divine name)

16.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
16.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

17.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
17.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

18.meaning: It became due / proved true / was justly confirmed — a verb meaning a thing has been established as a binding truth or a deserved, settled reality.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb with a doubled final letter. The -t ending marks a feminine subject ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine noun such as 'the word/decree.' It conveys that something has been confirmed as true and rightly due — established and inescapable.
18.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right; to be true, become due, be confirmed

19.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
19.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

20.meaning: Error, misguidance, straying — the state of having lost or wandered off the right path, the opposite of guidance.
20.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the straying') with the article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilating into 'ḍ'). The final '-u' is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or otherwise stands in that base state.
20.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, err

21.meaning: So travel! / then journey! — a command to a group (masculine 'you all') to set out and move across the land. The 'fa-' gives the sense 'so / then', tying the command to what came before.
21.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you all', prefixed by 'fa-' ('so/then'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressees being told to act. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter surfaces as the long 'ī' in this form.
21.root: س-ي-ر (s-y-r) — to travel, journey, move along; a journey

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
22.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

23.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
23.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

24.meaning: So look! / observe! — a command to a group to look, gaze, and consider; to direct one's sight and attention so as to see and reflect. The opening 'so/then' links the command to what precedes.
24.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, prefixed with fa- ('so/then'). The -ū ending aims the order at a masculine plural 'you' ('you all, look!'). The initial helping vowel (u-) appears because the bare stem would otherwise begin with two consonants together.
24.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

25.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
25.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

26.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

26.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

27.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
27.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
27.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

28.meaning: The deniers / those who cry lies — people who reject the truth as false and treat the messengers and revelation as lies. The word names them by their habit of calling truth a falsehood.
28.grammar: An active participle of Form II (the doubled, intensive pattern) in the sound masculine plural, made definite by 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, meaning 'the ones who…'; here it typically follows a possessive link ('the … of the deniers'). The Form II shape conveys persistently and emphatically declaring something a lie.
28.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; to declare false, give the lie to

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: You strive eagerly / are keen — to be greedy or intensely eager for something, to covet it and exert oneself to attain it; ardent desire combined with effort.
2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular subject ('you are eager / you covet'). The bare, vowelless ending (-∅) reflects the jussive/apocopate mood, the clipped form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'if' or a negation like 'do not'.
2.root: ح-ر-ص (ḥ-r-ṣ) — to be eager, keen, greedy; to covet

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: Their being guided / their guidance — the right direction and rightly-guided state, the act or condition of being led onto the correct path, joined with 'their.'
4.grammar: A noun ('guidance') with the attached pronoun -hum ('their,' for a masculine group). The noun ends in a long -ā (a fixed final vowel that does not change for case), and the pronoun -hum marks possession — 'the guidance OF them' = 'their guidance.'
4.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to show the right way

5.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
5.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
9.root: — (pronoun)

10.meaning: He lets go astray / leads astray — to cause someone to lose the way, to misguide and let them wander from the right path; the opposite of guiding.

parts.en: to lead/let go astray (Form IV stem)

10.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the -u ending signals the indicative mood (a plain statement). Form IV makes the verb causative — causing another to stray. The doubled l shows the root's second and third letters merged.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost; (Form IV) to lead/let astray

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
11.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

12.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: Helpers / supporters: those who give aid, support, and victory to another, standing by them against an adversary; the plural of 'helper'.
14.grammar: A masculine plural active participle — a 'doer' word meaning 'ones who help'. The sound plural ending -īna marks more than two; this -īna form (rather than -ūna) is the case used for objects of verbs and after prepositions or in possession (the accusative/genitive).
14.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to give victory/support

1.meaning: and they swore / took a solemn oath. From a root tied to dividing and apportioning, and so to swearing — calling something to witness in a binding vow.
1.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The ending -ū marks a masculine plural subject 'they.' (The written alif after it is silent.) Past tense presents the oath as already made.
1.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to divide, apportion; to swear an oath

2.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
2.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
2.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

3.meaning: Utmost effort, the full extent or strength of something; with 'oaths' it means the most solemn, strenuous oaths one can swear. The word denotes exertion pushed to its limit.
3.grammar: A noun in the accusative state (final -a). This case is taken by an object of a verb or, as often with this word, by a noun used adverbially or in a binding (genitive) construction with what follows — conveying 'with the utmost of …'.
3.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to strive, exert utmost effort

4.meaning: Their oaths; the solemn sworn pledges belonging to them. (The same plural form also serves the unrelated sense 'right hands', from which the oath sense derives, since oaths were sealed with the right hand.)
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural joined to the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel before the pronoun reflects the genitive state — the form taken when the noun follows a preposition or is bound to a preceding noun ('… of …'); -him marks the owners as a male/mixed group.
4.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; hence oath, and good fortune

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: He raises / resurrects / sends forth — to rouse and raise up, to dispatch or send out, and especially to bring the dead back to life and raise them up.
6.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the -u ending signals the indicative mood (a straightforward statement of fact).
6.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to raise up, send forth, resurrect

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
7.root: — (proper divine name)

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

9.meaning: He/it dies — to die, to lose life and pass away; the cessation of life.
9.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the -u ending signals the indicative mood (a plain statement). The long ū comes from a weak middle root letter (w) that surfaces as a vowel.
9.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — to die; death

10.meaning: Yes indeed / nay, rather — an affirmative reply used specifically to contradict a preceding negative and assert the positive: 'Yes (it is so), on the contrary.'
10.grammar: A response particle. Unlike a plain 'yes', it is used to overturn a negative statement or question and affirm what was denied. It does not inflect; the final long '-ā' is part of its fixed form.

11.meaning: A promise / a pledge — a binding commitment to do something, here in the sense of a solemn assurance given.
11.grammar: A masculine singular verbal noun, indefinite and in the accusative case, shown by the '-an' ending (nunation written over an alif). The accusative often marks a direct object or, as with such verbal nouns, an emphatic confirmation ('… as a promise / a sure promise').
11.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge

12.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
12.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

13.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
13.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
13.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

14.meaning: A connective particle 'but / however / yet' used to correct or contrast with what precedes, here with emphasis. It introduces a clause that sets the record straight against an expectation.
14.grammar: A contrastive conjunction ('but, however') joined by 'wa' ('and'). This is the heavy, emphatic form 'lākinna', which governs the noun after it into the object ('-a') case and adds force, like saying 'but in fact …'. It rebuts or qualifies a preceding statement.
14.root: — (no triliteral root; a compound particle of exception/contrast)

15.meaning: 'More' / 'greater (in number or amount)' — the comparative/superlative form built from 'much, many', meaning more numerous or more abundant.
15.grammar: A comparative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more …'). The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is an object or otherwise governed; this pattern does not take nunation. It is typically completed by 'than …'.
15.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much/many, abundance

16.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
16.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
16.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: 'So that He may make clear / explain plainly' — to clarify, distinguish, and set forth distinctly so that nothing remains obscure.

parts.en: so that / in order to (purpose particle)

1.grammar: Purpose particle li- ('so that, in order that') + a present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('He makes clear'). The doubled middle letter (bayyana) is an intensive/causative form: 'to make plain, clarify'. Because of the li- particle, the verb takes the subjunctive -a ending, giving the sense 'so that He may make clear' rather than a flat 'He makes clear'.
