1.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness; to be clear, to make evident

2.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

3.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they differ, disagree, or diverge from one another' — to hold conflicting views or take opposing courses; from a root tied to variance and succession.
4.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb in Form VIII (iftaʿala), which often carries a reflexive/reciprocal sense — here mutual differing. The prefix 'ya-' with the ending '-ūna' marks 'they' (masculine plural); the retained -na shows the indicative mood (an ongoing or factual action).
4.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, to differ, succession and divergence

5.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

6.meaning: 'So that He may make known/known-by-experience' — to bring something to light and distinguish it through what actually happens, so it becomes manifest and proven (a knowing tied to outcome, not the mere awareness already possessed).
6.grammar: Prefix wa- ('and') + purpose particle li- ('so that') + a present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('He knows/makes evident'). The li- of purpose puts the verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending, which is the form used after 'so that / in order to'.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

9.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
9.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

10.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
10.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

11.meaning: 'Liars / ones who lie' — people characterised by speaking falsehood.
11.grammar: An active participle ('one who lies') on the 'fāʿil' pattern, in the sound masculine plural. The '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case — the form used when the word is an object or otherwise not the subject.
11.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — lying, falsehood, denying the truth

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: Our word / our saying — speech, an utterance, or a statement, here belonging to 'us'; what is said or decreed by the speaker(s).
2.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive -nā ('our'), so 'our word / our saying'. The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically identifies the noun as the subject (the doer or topic) of its clause.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; a word, saying

3.meaning: To a thing / for a thing — directed toward some single, unspecified entity or matter; 'thing' in its broadest sense, anything that can be willed or referred to, with the prefix giving the sense 'to / for'.
3.grammar: A preposition li- ('to / for') joined to an indefinite noun. The -in ending (tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a/some') and the genitive case — the case a noun takes after a preposition like li- ('to a thing / for a thing').

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

5.meaning: A first-person plural past-tense verb meaning 'we willed / we intended / we purposed,' with an attached object pronoun 'it.' It conveys a settled act of will directing something to come about.
5.grammar: Past-tense (completed action) verb in Form IV (the af'ala pattern, which often makes a verb causative or purposive). Because the root is hollow (its middle letter is a weak wāw), the pattern does not surface as the regular 'af'ala'; the middle wāw contracts to a long 'ā', giving 'arāda' rather than 'arwada'. The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we'; the final '-hu' is an attached object pronoun, 'it/him.'
5.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, desire, will, go after something

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: A first-person plural present/future verb meaning 'we say / we utter / we declare.' It denotes the act of speaking or pronouncing words.
7.grammar: Present-tense verb with the 'na-' prefix marking the doer as 'we.' The final '-a' (instead of the usual '-u') is the subjunctive ending, the mood used after certain particles meaning 'that / so that / in order to.'
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

8.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
8.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

9.meaning: The command 'Be!' — an order to come into existence, the creative imperative by which a thing is summoned into being.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'Be!' It is the shortened command form of the verb 'to be/become,' with the bare, vowel-less ending typical of a singular order.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

10.meaning: A connective particle 'and' joined to a present-tense verb 'it is / it comes to be.' Together they express something coming into existence or a state taking effect.
10.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'and then / so,' marking a result or sequence. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/it'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, the mood of a plain statement of fact ('it is / it comes to be').
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come into being

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They emigrated / migrated — they left their homes and abandoned a place, especially departing for the sake of faith.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the mutual/effortful (form III) pattern, carrying the sense of cutting oneself off from one's home and people by migrating. The -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural) as the doers of a completed action. (The written final alif is a silent spelling convention.)

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
6.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
6.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: A third-person plural past-tense passive verb meaning 'they were wronged / treated unjustly / oppressed.' It marks people as the recipients of injustice done to them.
8.grammar: Past-tense passive verb (the internal vowel pattern u-i signals 'the action was done to them, not by them'). The '-ū' ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural), here the ones to whom the wrong was done.
8.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression, putting something out of its rightful place

9.meaning: An emphatic promise: 'We will most certainly settle them / give them a dwelling-place / establish them,' with an attached pronoun 'them.' It speaks of granting a secure place or standing.
9.grammar: The opening 'la-' is an emphatic particle ('surely, certainly'). The 'nu-' prefix marks the doer as 'we.' This is a Form II verb (the doubled-middle pattern, often intensive/causative: 'to settle someone'). The doubled '-nna' is the heavy emphatic ending that strengthens a promise or threat; the final '-hum' is the attached object pronoun 'them.'
9.root: ب-و-أ (b-w-') — to settle in a place, take up a dwelling, give an abode

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
11.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

12.meaning: Something good, fine, or beautiful; a good deed, a benefit, or a blessing. As a noun it denotes a good thing or good fortune.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective (the -a marks feminine gender). The final -tan (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a good thing') and in the accusative case, typically used for the direct object of a verb or as the thing requested/described.
12.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, fine

13.meaning: And surely the reward / wage / recompense. The noun ajr (a due reward or payment for one's deeds or work) carries a prefixed 'and' plus an emphatic 'surely', stressing the certainty of the recompense.
13.grammar: A noun carrying two prefixes — wa- ('and') and the emphatic la- ('surely') — that together open and stress the statement. The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or the thing being asserted ('and surely the reward is…').
13.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — to reward, recompense; a wage or due reward

14.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
14.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
14.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

15.meaning: Greater, bigger, more grave — the comparative/superlative 'more great' or 'greatest'.
15.grammar: An elative on the afʿal pattern, expressing 'more/most great'. Such forms are diptotes, so they take -u (without nunation) in the nominative; the -u marks it as a subject or predicate ('is greater').
15.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness

16.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
16.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

17.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
17.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

18.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: 'They were patient / they endured steadfastly / they persevered.' The verb means to restrain oneself, to bear hardship with calm endurance, to hold firm and not give way to panic or complaint. Ṣabr is steadfast, self-controlled perseverance.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) in the masculine plural 'they' person. The stem ṣabar- carries the completed-action (past) sense. The -ū ending marks the doers as 'they' (masculine plural) who performed the act ('they were patient / they endured'). The written alif after it is a silent spelling convention that regularly follows the plural -ū on a verb and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A compound, 'and upon / and on / and against' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, against'). It adds a further thing onto which something rests or against which it bears.
3.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and', joining what follows to what came before. ʿalā is an indeclinable preposition that puts the following noun in the genitive case and signals 'on, over, or upon' something.

4.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
4.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

5.meaning: They place their reliance and trust, committing their affairs to another and depending wholly upon Him. Conveys active, ongoing dependence and entrusting of outcomes.
5.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb from Form V (reflexive: 'to make oneself rely'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject doing the action now or habitually ('they rely'). The -na also signals the verb is in its full, uninterrupted form.
5.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, appoint as guardian, rely upon; committing one's affairs to another.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
4.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: Men — the plural of 'man' (an adult male); also carries the sense of menfolk as distinct from women.
6.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa). This ending typically signals the word is a direct object, or names something brought about/scattered ('[He made/produced] men…').

7.meaning: "we reveal / we send down by inspiration" — an ongoing or repeated act of disclosing something to a recipient, especially conveying a message or revelation, expressed in the 'we' voice.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the derived (Form IV) causative pattern (to cause a message to reach someone). The nu- prefix marks the doer as 'we'. The long -ī at the end is the bare present-tense form, signalling an action that is ongoing, habitual, or yet to be completed.
7.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, inspire, signal swiftly

8.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
8.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
8.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: A connective 'so / then' joined to a plural command 'ask! / inquire! / question!' It directs a group of people to seek information by asking.
9.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'so / then,' linking to what precedes. The verb is a command (imperative) addressed to a group; the '-ū' ending marks the addressees as 'you all' (masculine plural).
9.root: س-أ-ل (s-'-l) — to ask, inquire, request, question

10.meaning: People of / folk of — the people belonging to something, its members or family; those who hold or are associated with a thing (a place, a faith, a household).
10.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of …,' normally joined to a following noun ('the people OF …'). The final -a (fatḥa) is the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or after certain particles.
10.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to something

11.meaning: 'The reminder / the remembrance / the admonition' — a noun for a message that recalls truth to mind, often used of revealed scripture as that which reminds people of Allah.
11.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically signals a link to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or that the word follows a preposition.
11.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind, remind

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
13.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
15.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.
15.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

1.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
1.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'

2.meaning: And the scriptures / written records — the plural of a written page or book; revealed writings or recorded texts.
2.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article 'al-' (the) and the connector 'wa' (and). The final '-i' (kasra) is the definite genitive: it typically follows a preposition or oath particle, or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain.
2.root: ز-ب-ر (z-b-r) — to write; a written piece

3.meaning: 'And we sent down' — to cause something to descend or come down from a higher place, often used of sending down rain, sustenance, or revelation. Prefixed with 'and' and marked for a 'we' subject in the past.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (meaning 'to make come down'). The suffix -nā marks 'we' as the doer, giving 'we sent down'. The wa- prefix is 'and'. The causative form distinguishes it from simply 'descending' — it means causing descent.

4.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
4.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

5.meaning: The Reminder: an admonition or message that recalls the heart to what it should not forget — guidance, remembrance of Allah, and one of the names of the Qur'an itself as that which reminds.
5.grammar: A definite verbal noun (maṣdar). The -a ending is accusative: it typically marks the word as a direct object — the thing being followed, remembered, or sent.
5.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

6.meaning: A purpose phrase 'so that you may make clear / explain / clarify / set forth distinctly.' It denotes the act of clearly expounding something so it is understood.
6.grammar: The prefix 'li-' means 'so that / in order to,' expressing purpose. The 'tu-' prefix marks a second-person singular doer ('you'). This is a Form II verb (doubled-middle, intensive/causative: 'to make clear'). The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending required after 'li-' ('that you may …').
6.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making plain, separating out

7.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.
7.root: ن-و-س / ا-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: A past-tense passive verb meaning 'it was sent down / caused to descend' — something made to come down (typically revelation), with an intensive nuance of being sent down gradually or fully.
9.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) passive verb of Form II (the doubled-middle pattern, which adds intensity or gradualness), 3rd-person masculine singular. The vowel shape 'nuzzila' (u–i) marks it as passive: the subject is the thing acted upon, with the doer unnamed ('it was sent down'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.
9.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (sending down)

10.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
10.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
10.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: And so that they may / and perhaps they will. The particle laʿalla expresses hope or expectation that something may come about ('it may be that…'), often introducing a hoped-for purpose; attached to 'them' and joined to a preceding word by 'and'.

parts.en: perhaps, so that, it may be that

11.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps / so that') is one that puts the following noun in the accusative; the attached -hum ('they') is therefore its accusative subject. It conveys hope, expectation, or a hoped-for outcome. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
11.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: They reflect / ponder — to think deeply and turn a matter over in the mind, considering it carefully.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they reflect.' The intensive pattern (with the doubled middle root letter) conveys careful, repeated mental effort. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural doer ('they') in the ordinary (indicative) mood.
12.root: ف-ك-ر (f-k-r) — to think, ponder, reflect

1.meaning: So, did [they] then feel secure? — a verb of feeling safe and free from fear, fronted by question and connective particles. 'Amina' means to be safe, to trust, to feel no apprehension of harm.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb fronted by two particles: the interrogative a- ('did …?') opening a question, and the connective fa- ('then, so') linking to what precedes. The verb's -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') having completed the action.
1.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, freedom from fear

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They plotted / schemed — to devise a hidden plan or stratagem against someone, working secretly to bring about an outcome.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The ending -ū means 'they (all)' did the action — a completed act of scheming by a group. (The written alif after the wāw is silent.) The root denotes covert planning, which may be blameworthy or, when ascribed to Allah, a just outmaneuvering of such plots.
3.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to plot, scheme, devise a stratagem

4.meaning: 'The evil deeds / bad actions' — plural of sayyi'a, a wrong or evil act, a misdeed or sin; the opposite of a good deed.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the misdeeds'). The -i ending here is the case marker for the sound feminine plural in the genitive/accusative state, typically signalling that it follows a preposition, links to a preceding noun, or stands as an object.
4.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; misdeed, wrong

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: 'That He should cause (the ground) to cave in and swallow up.' The verb means to make land sink and collapse, sucking down whatever is on it, as in an earthquake or a sinkhole.

parts.en: (that) he — ya- prefix doubled by assimilation of a preceding 'an'
cause to sink and swallow up

6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the subjunctive. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it'). It is written with a shadda (doubled, 'yya-') because a preceding particle 'an' ('that / lest') loses its final 'n', which assimilates (idghām) into the 'y'; so 'an ya-' is pronounced and written 'a-yya-'. The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending required after that particle, giving 'that he should…' rather than a plain statement.
6.root: خ-س-ف (kh-s-f) — to sink, cave in, be swallowed by the earth

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
7.root: — (proper divine name)

8.meaning: 'By/with them' or 'for them' — the preposition bi ('with, by, through, for') joined to the attached pronoun 'them' (a masculine group).
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, for') attached to the pronoun -him ('them', masculine plural). The final -u is a connecting vowel added so the word joins smoothly to whatever follows. The preposition naturally puts its pronoun in the genitive.

9.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'
9.root: أ-ر-ض (ʼ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

10.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
10.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

11.meaning: it comes to them / that it come to them; a verb expressing arrival or coming upon a group of people, with those people as the object reached.
11.grammar: Present-tense verb (from a defective root ending in a weak letter) with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine subject ('he/it'). In the segment -ya, the -y is the verb's final root letter and the -a is the subjunctive marker, which appears after a particle such as 'that', 'until', or 'so that', expressing a hoped-for or pending action. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them', its final vowel given as -u before a following word.
11.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

12.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
12.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.
12.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
13.root: — (preposition)

14.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
14.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

15.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
15.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'they perceive / they are aware / they sense.' The root denotes fine, immediate awareness — noticing or feeling something, often subconsciously. It frequently appears in the negative, expressing that people fail to realize something.

parts.en: perceive / sense / be aware (Form I stem)

16.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form I (imperfect stem yashʿuru, with -u- after the second root letter), third-person masculine plural. The prefix 'ya-' and ending -ūna give 'they (masc.) do / are doing,' the -ūna marking the indicative — an ongoing or habitual state of awareness (or, when negated, the lack of it).
16.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense, be finely aware

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

2.meaning: A present/future verb 'that He may seize / grasp / take hold of' with an attached pronoun 'them.' It conveys a sudden, gripping act of taking, often in the sense of overtaking with punishment.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb with the 'ya-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular doer ('He'). The final '-a' (rather than '-u') is the subjunctive ending, used after particles meaning 'that / so that / lest.' The attached '-hum' is the object pronoun 'them.'
2.root: أ-خ-ذ ('-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp, take hold of

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: A verbal noun meaning 'their moving about / turning to and fro / going back and forth,' with an attached pronoun 'their.' It captures restless coming-and-going or fluctuation from one state to another.

parts.en: moving about / turning to and fro

4.grammar: A verbal noun of Form V (the 'tafa''ul' pattern, often reflexive/repeated action: 'turning oneself about repeatedly'). The '-i' before the suffix is the genitive ending (the word follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun); the attached '-him' is the possessive pronoun 'their.'
4.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, overturn, flip, change from one state to another

5.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
5.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

6.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
6.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

7.meaning: Active participle meaning 'ones who render (something) powerless / unable to be caught', i.e. those who frustrate or thwart a pursuer and escape beyond reach. The prefixed 'bi-' is a preposition often used to govern such a predicate.
7.grammar: A plural active participle from a causative verb meaning 'to render incapable, to frustrate'. The '-īna' ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive state ('ones who…'). The attached 'bi-' is a preposition; here it precedes the predicate, a common construction giving the sense 'are not able to thwart/escape'.
7.root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z) — inability, incapacity, weakness

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

2.meaning: A present/future verb 'that He may seize / grasp / take hold of' with an attached pronoun 'them.' It conveys a sudden, gripping act of taking, often in the sense of overtaking with punishment.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb with the 'ya-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular doer ('He'). The final '-a' (rather than '-u') is the subjunctive ending, used after particles meaning 'that / so that / lest.' The attached '-hum' is the object pronoun 'them.'
2.root: أ-خ-ذ ('-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp, take hold of

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: An indefinite noun meaning 'a gradual diminishing / a state of fear / a wearing-away through dread.' It denotes either fearfulness itself or a slow erosion brought on while in fear.
4.grammar: A verbal noun of Form V (the 'tafa''ul' pattern, suggesting a process that builds up gradually). The final '-in' (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: '-i' marks the genitive (after a preposition or linking to a noun), and the '-n' sound marks it as indefinite ('a …').

5.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
5.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

6.meaning: Your Lord — the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, owns, and cares for you, guiding His servants to completion. "Rabb" carries the joined senses of owner, sustainer, and the one who lovingly brings to maturity, here addressed to a group.
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun with an attached possessive "your" (plural addressee). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, bring to completion

7.meaning: Truly most kind, compassionate, tender; one who shows raʾfa — gentle pity and clemency, an especially soft and caring form of mercy. Used as a divine attribute.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿūl ('full of kindness'), with the emphatic prefix la- ('truly'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case combined with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is truly most kind').
7.root: ر-أ-ف (r-ʾ-f) — tender compassion, clemency, pity

8.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
1.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

2.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
3.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
5.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
8.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
8.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

9.meaning: A present-tense verb 'it inclines / turns / shifts back and forth,' used of shadows leaning and moving. It describes something gradually swinging or turning from side to side.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb of Form V (the 'tafa''ul' pattern, here a continuous/repeated turning). The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person doer ('it/they'). It carries a shaddah (doubling mark) because a preceding 'n' sound (from a connector ending in nūn) has been assimilated into the 'y', so the two merge and are written as one doubled 'yy'. The stem is 'tafayya'u'; the final '-u' is the indicative ending (a plain statement of an ongoing action). The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention written after the final long vowel and is not pronounced.
9.root: ف-ي-أ (f-y-') — to return, turn back, shade; relating to shade that shifts

10.meaning: 'Its shadows / shades' — the plural noun for shadows, with an attached pronoun 'its.' A shadow is the dark shape cast when something blocks light.
10.grammar: A plural noun ('shadows') with an attached possessive pronoun. The '-u' before the suffix is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the doer or subject of its clause; the attached '-hu' means 'its/his.'
10.root: ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l) — shade, shadow, shelter, lasting coolness

11.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

12.meaning: "the right (side/hand)" — the right-hand direction, often carrying overtones of strength, good fortune, and honor.
12.grammar: A definite noun ("the …" via al-) carrying the -i (genitive) ending, which typically marks it as following a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ("… of the right").
12.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — the right side; good fortune, blessing

13.meaning: A connective 'and' joined to 'the lefts / the left sides' — the plural of the left-hand side or direction.
13.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and.' The noun carries the definite article 'al-' ('the') and is a broken (internal) plural ('left sides'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, signaling a link to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or that the word follows a preposition.
13.root: ش-م-ل (sh-m-l) — the left side / left hand; also to encompass, include

14.meaning: 'Prostrating' / 'in prostration' — bowing down low with the face to the ground, the posture of deepest humility and worship. A plural describing a group in that humble, bowed state.
14.grammar: A plural active descriptor ('those prostrating'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, which here works adverbially — describing the manner or state in which the subject acts (i.e. doing something 'while prostrating'). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive plural pattern used for a group performing the action.
14.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

15.meaning: 'To / for Allah' — the preposition 'to/for' (expressing belonging, purpose, or recipient) joined to the name Allah, conveying that something belongs to or is due to Allah.
15.grammar: The prefixed preposition li- ('to/for', also marking possession or purpose) attached to the proper name Allah. After this preposition the name takes the genitive (its -i ending), the case used for the object of a preposition and for showing belonging.
15.root: — (proper name)

16.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
16.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

17.meaning: A masculine plural describing those who are 'lowly / humbled / submissive / abased.' It marks a group as bowing low in humility before a greater authority.
17.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer/be-er' word: 'ones who are lowly') in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending marks it as masculine plural and nominative, the case that typically marks the subject or describes the subject of a clause.
17.root: د-خ-ر (d-kh-r) — to be lowly, humble, abased, submissive

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'he/it prostrates, bows down in submission'; it denotes lowering oneself to the ground in worship and humble obedience — the deepest posture of submission before Allah.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, the plain-statement form used when no particle governs the verb to change its ending.
2.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in worship

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
9.root: — (preposition)

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'a moving/walking creature / a beast / any living thing that treads the earth' — broadly, any animal that moves along the ground.
10.grammar: A singular indefinite feminine noun (originally an active participle, 'one that moves/treads'). The ending -tin combines the feminine marker (tā' marbūṭa) with tanwīn showing indefiniteness and the genitive case — the form typically used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …'). The final '-n' sound is spoken but unwritten.
10.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move/creep/walk gently along the ground

11.meaning: A connective 'and' joined to 'the angels' — the plural noun for angels, the unseen servants of Allah created to carry out His commands.
11.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and.' The noun carries the definite article 'al-' ('the') and is a plural ('angels'). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the doer or subject of its clause.
11.root: ل-أ-ك (l-'-k) — relating to message/messengership (an angel as a bearer of Allah's command)

12.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
12.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

13.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

14.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they act arrogantly, deem themselves great, behave with haughty pride' — to puff oneself up and disdain to submit or yield.
14.grammar: A present-tense (form X) verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending signals the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact. Form X here carries the sense of considering oneself great.
14.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness; here, self-magnification and pride

1.meaning: They fear: to be afraid of, to hold in awe or dread. Often used of reverent fear of Allah as well as ordinary fear of danger.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form I (with a weak middle letter, giving the long ā), third-person masculine plural ('they fear'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject; the full -ūna ending (with its final -na intact) marks a plural of males in the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact.

2.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: Above them / over them — the place or position over the top of someone or something, joined to 'them'.
4.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'above/over,' commonly used to mean 'over …'. The -i (kasra) is the genitive ending, here triggered by the following possessor; the attached '-him' is 'them' (its vowel is 'hi' after an -i sound).
4.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above; aboveness, superiority

5.meaning: A connective 'and' joined to a third-person plural verb 'they do / they act / they carry out.' It denotes the performing of deeds or actions.
5.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and.' The present-tense verb has a 'ya-' prefix plus '-ūna' ending, which together mark a third-person masculine plural doer ('they'). In the middle segment the fā' carries a sukūn (no vowel of its own), so it is read 'f' joined straight to the following 'alū' — the stem segment is pronounced 'f'alū'. The retained '-na' shows the indicative mood, the form of a plain statement of fact ('they do').
5.root: ف-ع-ل (f-'-l) — to do, act, make, perform

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A third-person plural present-tense passive verb 'they are commanded / ordered / bidden.' It marks people as the recipients of a command given to them.
7.grammar: Present-tense passive verb (the 'yu-…-u' vowelling signals 'the action is done to them'). The 'yu-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), here the ones being commanded. The retained '-na' shows the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact).
7.root: أ-م-ر ('-m-r) — to command, order, bid, instruct

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.

5.meaning: 'Two gods / two deities' — the dual of 'ilāh' (a god, an object of worship), i.e., exactly two such objects of worship.
5.grammar: A dual noun (exactly two). The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the object/genitive state (used as a non-subject or after a preposition), as opposed to the subject-form dual ending '-āni'.
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — to worship, deify; (ilāh) a god, that which is worshipped

6.meaning: Two; the cardinal number 2 (in its masculine dual form), denoting a matched pair.
6.grammar: The number 'two' in dual form. The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive case — the shape used when the word is an object or follows a preposition. The initial 'i' is a helping vowel (a 'connecting hamza') that smooths pronunciation.
6.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — twoness, doubling, a second of a pair

7.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
7.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

8.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
8.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

9.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
9.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

10.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
10.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.

11.meaning: A connective 'so / and' joined to an emphatic, isolated object pronoun meaning 'Me alone / Me in particular.' The special form 'iyyā-' with an attached pronoun singles out the object for exclusive emphasis ('it is Me, and none else').
11.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'so / then.' 'Iyyā' is a special carrier used to put an object pronoun first for emphasis or exclusivity; the attached '-ya' is the first-person singular pronoun 'me.' Fronting an object this way typically conveys 'Me alone / it is Me specifically.'
11.root: — (particle of emphasis; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: 'So fear / stand in awe of Me' — a command to feel reverent dread and awe, to hold something in fearful reverence. Prefixed 'fa' means 'so/then.'
12.grammar: 'So/then' (fa) plus a command verb to a masculine plural 'you,' followed by an object 'me.' The '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all fear!'). The final '-ni' is the 'protective nūn' (nūn al-wiqāya), a nūn inserted to shield the verb's ending before a first-person object; the actual object pronoun 'me' (-ī) is elided after it, so the '-ni' itself carries the sense 'me.'
12.root: ر-ه-ب (r-h-b) — fear mixed with awe, dread, reverence

1.meaning: And for him / and he has — the connector 'and', the preposition 'for/to', and the pronoun 'him'. Together it expresses possession or belonging ('and to him belongs …', 'and he has …').
1.grammar: A small phrase, not a verb: the connector wa- ('and') + the preposition la- ('for/to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). The preposition with a pronoun commonly conveys having or belonging ('he has', 'belonging to him').

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
5.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

6.meaning: 'And for Him / and to Him belongs' — the preposition 'for/to' expressing belonging or possession, joined with the pronoun 'Him.' It conveys that something belongs or is due to Him.
6.grammar: A small phrase: the connector 'and' plus the preposition la- ('for, to, belonging to') with the attached pronoun -hu ('Him'). The construction 'la- + pronoun' expresses possession or entitlement — 'and to Him belongs …' / 'and for Him is …'

7.meaning: A noun, 'the dīn.' Dīn spans religion, faith, the way of life one follows in obedience, and also judgement, reckoning, and recompense — the system of accountability and devotion one lives by and answers to.
7.grammar: A definite noun marked by al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or main topic of a sentence (the one doing or being something).
7.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, judgement, recompense

8.meaning: An indefinite descriptive word meaning 'lasting / constant / perpetual / unceasing.' It describes something that continues without interruption and is rightfully due at all times.
8.grammar: An active participle (a 'be-er' word: 'that which is constant/lasting') used descriptively. The final '-an' (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending: the '-a' marks the accusative case (often the role of an object or a descriptive state, 'being constant'), and the '-n' sound marks it as indefinite.
8.root: و-ص-ب (w-ṣ-b) — to be lasting, constant, perpetual, enduring

9.meaning: A pointed question meaning roughly 'so is it other than…?' — combining a 'then/so' connector, a questioning particle expressing surprise or rebuke, and the word 'other than / besides.'
9.grammar: A compound: the questioning particle a- (asking 'is it…?', often with a tone of astonishment or reproach) joined to the connector fa- ('then/so'), prefixed to the noun 'ghayr' (other/something else). The -a ending on ghayra is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or after certain particles.
9.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, change

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: 'you become mindful and guard yourselves,' 'you are God-conscious' — to shield oneself through reverent awareness of Allah, guarding against wrongdoing and His displeasure. This is the verb of taqwā: a protective, careful piety, not merely 'fear.'
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of the self-protective (form VIII) pattern. The 'ta-' prefix marks 'you,' and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine subject ('you all') in the ongoing/indicative mood — the full '-ūna' (rather than shortened '-ū') signals the plain indicative, stating an action as a fact or expected reality.
11.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect (basis of taqwā)

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
2.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').
